sections.html:
Auburn sits in western Lee County in eastern Alabama, with Opelika to the northeast. It is the principal city of the Auburn metropolitan area, which counted 193,773 residents in 2020. The city proper has grown to nearly three times its 1980 size, and its 2020 population was 76,143. Auburn University, the largest employer with 13,545 people on staff in 2024, drives much of the housing demand.

Measure, 2020 censusAuburn
Population76,143
Median age24.6 years
Households30,233
Housing units33,209 (9.0% vacant)
Homeowner vacancy rate2.0%
Rental vacancy rate6.0%

A median age of 24.6 means a large share of homes are rented to students. Many owners are investors or parents who bought a house for a child and now want out. Those owners tend to share a worry: a tenant on a lease, furniture still inside and a school year that will not wait.

The university calendar moves the local market. On home game weekends the city can see more than 100,000 visitors, and Jordan-Hare Stadium seats 87,451. A house close to campus can look very different on game day than it does in July, with parked cars, traffic and noise all around it.

If you are listing, schedule viewings around the home schedule and tell buyers what to expect on those weekends. If you are selling for cash, mention the location and the rental history, because a buyer wants to know both. A direct sale also removes the problem of arranging showings around a crowded fall.

Auburn City Schools has 14 campuses and more than 9,400 students. It includes ten elementary schools, two middle schools, a junior high and one high school, and a second high school is planned to open in August 2028. Elementary zones come in pairs: one school serves kindergarten through second grade and the other third through fifth.

Families ask about school zoning before almost anything else. Have the zone for your address ready when you describe the house.

sections.h2: Weather and what to check before you sell
sections.html:
The climate is humid subtropical, with about 52.6 inches of rain a year. Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind or large hail are common from late winter through early summer, tornadoes are a risk, and Hurricanes Opal in 1995 and Ivan in 2004 sent heavy rain and wind through the area. Walk the property before you list or sell and look at:

  • Roof age and hail damage on shingles, vents and gutters.
  • Water staining on ceilings or around windows after heavy rain.
  • Drainage near the foundation, which matters on a hilly lot.
  • Large trees near the house, garage or power line.

Auburn sits on the Fall Line, where the Piedmont plateau meets the coastal plain, and elevation runs from 386 feet at Chewacla Creek to 845 feet near the Chambers County line. Two houses in the same city can face very different slope, soil and water.

  • Southwest and west: rolling plains.
  • South: coastal plain with sandy soil and pine forest.
  • North: thick forest, high hills and deep hollows.
  • Three creek systems drain the city: Chewacla and Opintlocco, Saugahatchee, and Sandy Creek.

Mention standing water, erosion or a steep driveway if your lot has them. Buyers find those flaws on a first visit, and hearing about them from you first is better than discovering them alone.

sections.h2: Utilities, inspections and who to call
sections.html:
Auburn is reached by Interstate 85, US 29 and US 280. It is heavily car-dependent, with no city bus system. Atlanta and Birmingham are each within about two hours, and Auburn University Regional Airport serves general aviation.

  • Water and sewer: the Water Works Board of Auburn.
  • Electricity: Alabama Power.
  • Trash and recycling: Auburn Environmental Services.
  • Construction inspections: the Codes Enforcement Division of the Public Safety Department.

Codes Enforcement monitors construction in the city. An unpermitted addition, garage conversion or extra bedroom is worth mentioning early with any buyer, and you can call the division to ask what was permitted on your address.

sections.h2: How a sale closes in Auburn
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the county probate judge, who calculates the state recording tax at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of that. It has to arrive with proof of the actual sale price, and a mortgage that already paid its own tax is subtracted first.

Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. If you close near those dates, ask the closing office who pays the current bill and how it will appear on the settlement statement.

  1. Request a mortgage payoff letter and the latest tax bill.
  2. Pull the deed, and confirm every owner can sign.
  3. For a rental, gather leases, deposit records and a rent roll.
  4. Choose a closing agent to search title and prepare the settlement statement.
  5. Record the deed and settle liens from proceeds.

A house rented to students raises questions a regular home does not. Start with the lease: who the tenants are, when it ends, how much deposit is held and whether the lease passes to a new owner. A buyer who plans to keep the tenants will want the rent roll and payment history. A buyer who wants the house empty will want to know how soon it can be.

Talk to your tenants early and honestly. Tenants who know a sale is coming and what it means for their lease are more likely to allow access and keep the house tidy. If the lease runs past your preferred closing date, ask whether the buyer will take the house with tenants in place, or whether a different closing date makes more sense.

Investors and parents who bought for a child often carry a mortgage and a tax bill but no longer want the work of managing repairs between semesters. In that situation the cash route has a clear appeal: no cleaning out, no staging and no showings while someone still lives there. The trade-off is price, so compare the offer with what the house could earn if you held it another year, and choose with that number in front of you.

Owners here usually choose among listing around the school calendar, selling to another investor or taking an as-is cash offer when a tenant, a repair list or a move date makes a listing hard. We buy houses in Auburn in their current condition and you pay no commission, so you can compare an offer with a listing before you commit.

A listing can bring a higher price for a house that shows well, but it asks for patience. Students move on a schedule, and a vacant house near campus loses value if it sits through a slow month. A cash buyer works to your date instead, and the closing can be set for the day your lease ends or your move begins. Get any offer in writing, ask who pays for title work and ask for the closing date before you agree.

faqs.q: Is Auburn, Alabama, in Lee County?
faqs.a: Yes. Auburn sits in western Lee County and is the principal city of the Auburn metropolitan area.

faqs.q: Does football season affect selling a house in Auburn?
faqs.a: It can. Home games bring crowds that can top 100,000 visitors, so showings, parking and traffic near campus change on those weekends. Plan viewing times around the schedule.
Auburn City Schools serves the city, with 14 campuses and more than 9,400 students. A second high school is planned to open in August 2028.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, with delinquency after December 31. Ask the closing office who pays the current year's bill when you sell.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Auburn rental house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell a house with or without tenants and without repairs. Keep the leases, deposit records and rent roll handy so the buyer and the closing office can review them.
